newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Wife of opposition politician may travel - Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Wife of opposition politician may travel - Singapore.

text.p: The wife of an opposition politician who has fled Singapore and faces massive damages for libel may now be permitted to travel, the Immigration Department said on Wednesday.
The move could open the way for Teo Siew Har to join her husband Tang Liang Hong, who also faces arrest on charges of tax evasion in Singapore.
Tang left Singapore in January, saying he had received death threats, after losing a bitterly contested general election fight that month.
A statement from Singapore's Immigration Department said Teo "may now be permitted to travel. Accordingly, she may apply to Singapore Immigration for her passport."
Teo was barred from leaving the country in January when she tried to cross into Malaysia. Officials said she was needed in Singapore to provide information on a tax investigation related to Tang.
Teo "has furnished the information requested of her", the Immigration Department statement said.

On May 29 a Singapore court awarded Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and senior colleagues in his ruling party a record Singapore $8.08 million (US$5.65 million) in libel damages from Tang, who had called them liars when they accused him of being "an anti-English education, anti-Christian Chinese chauvinist".
Tang has said he would appeal the damages, and has other appeals pending. Since leaving Singapore, he has been in Malaysia, Britain and Hong Kong.
He was also formally charged on May 23 with 33 counts of tax evasion, and a warrant was issued for his arrest.
Tang faces a fine of three times the amount of tax he is accused of evading -- S$211,000 -- plus a fine of S$10,000 on each charge. He could also be jailed for three years on each charge.
